Bessarabia stays Russian: an oblast from 1818 and a guberniya from 1873

successors.note: The end year 1813 follows Cliopatria's row, not an event: nothing on the pages opened ends Russian Bessarabia in 1813.

capitals.name: Chișinău (Kishinev)
capitals.note: The page calls Chișinău 'the former capital of the Russian Bessarabia Governorate' (1873); it is silent on the seat in 1812-1813.

correction.text: 'the Budjak and the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia, between Prut and Dniester Rivers', 45,630 km2, ceded to Russia on 28 May 1812

keyframe_review.note: The Cliopatria row (42,009 km2, bbox 25.02-28.24E, 45.30-48.26N, modern country Romania) is the Moldavian land WEST of the Prut: it has the same area and bbox as the Principality of Moldavia's 1814-1827 shape, covers Iasi and Cahul but not Chisinau (tools/gazetteer.py: 0 cells within 30 km of Chisinau, 4 cells within 20 km of Iasi), and the Moldavia row has no shape for 1812-1813. The page's Bessarabia is the land between the Prut and the Dniester (45,630 km2; ratio of Cliopatria's area to the page 0.92, but the outline is the wrong land). Use the region Bessarabia for this dossier and give the Cliopatria shape to principality-of-moldavia for 1812-1813. Cliopatria's Russian Empire shape already covers Chisinau from 1811.

region.text: the land between the Pruth and the Dniester: 'the Budjak and the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia, between Prut and Dniester Rivers'

ledger.note: 28 May 1812: the Treaty of Bucharest cedes Bessarabia to Russia. 'was signed on 28 May 1812, in Manuc's Inn in Bucharest' (ratified 5 July 1812); the ceded area is 'the Budjak and the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia, between Prut and Dniester Rivers', 45,630 km2.

region.text: the Budjak, under direct Ottoman rule before 1812

ledger.note: 28 May 1812: the Budjak passes from the Ottomans to Russia, 'ceded by the Ottoman Empire (to which Moldavia was a vassal) to Russia'. The Bessarabia page adds the Ottomans held 'direct rule only in Budjak and Khotyn' and that the Nogai tribes there were 'totally driven out prior to 1812'.

Cliopatria's row ends in 1813 and Cliopatria's Russian Empire shape covers the land throughout; the page is silent on any 1813 event. Bessarabia remains Russian: 'Administratively, Bessarabia became an oblast of the Russian Empire in 1818, and a guberniya in 1873.'

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)

zones.text: the land between the Pruth and the Dniester

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) concluded the war: the Ottoman Empire ceded the land between the Pruth and the Dniester to Russia, 'That entire region was then called Bessarabia.'
wars.note: The war's own article was not opened (page budget 1-2). The Bessarabia page says Russia 'occupied the region five times' in 1711-1812 without dating the occupations, so no contest events are recorded.

certainty.note: The pages give the Prut and Dniester as the limits of the ceded land but no surveyed line in the south (Danube mouths, Black Sea coast) or around Khotyn.

sources.title: Bessarabia
sources.note: Treaty of Bucharest 28 May 1812, Budjak and Khotyn under direct Ottoman rule, oblast 1818, guberniya 1873, 1856 and 1878 changes; no 1812 area figure of its own.

sources.title: Treaty of Bucharest (1812)
sources.note: Signed 28 May 1812, ratified 5 July 1812; ceded area (Budjak and eastern Moldavia between Prut and Dniester), 45,630 km2.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Bessarabia' row 1812-1813 is the wrong land: it is the Moldavian rump west of the Prut (same area and bbox as principality-of-moldavia_1814, which starts only in 1814); the eu-18 Moldavia dossier should take it for 1812-1813. This dossier therefore describes the ceded land with the gazetteer region 'Bessarabia' (45,630 km2 per the treaty page). Bessarabia was an annexed province, not a sovereign state: type colony of the Russian Empire, whose Cliopatria shape already covers Chisinau from 1811, so the land should be drawn as Russian territory (the renderer may prefer to drop this row). The end year 1813 follows Cliopatria and is not an event (confidence-1 dissolve). Not settled: Khotyn (page silent on its status after 1812) and the 1806-1812 occupation by dated stages. Pages not opened: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812), Bessarabia Governorate (budget).
